questions: Do you have a tremor, especially when your hands are at rest?
Have you noticed slowness in your daily activities (like getting dressed or eating)?
Have you experienced any falls or near-falls in the past year?
Do people tell you that you walk slowly or shuffle when you walk?
Do you ever feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when standing up from a sitting or lying position?
Do you have any trouble with your memory or thinking clearly?
Have you noticed any leakage of urine (incontinence)?
Do you take any medications that might affect your balance or blood pressure?
Do you have pain in your knees or hips when standing or walking?
Have you ever been diagnosed with arthritis or a joint problem?
Do you have any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet?
Has a doctor ever told you that your blood pressure drops when you stand up?
Do you have trouble seeing clearly?
Have you ever had a stroke or TIA (mini-stroke)?
Do you feel unsteady or off-balance when you turn around quickly?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a problem with the inner ear (like vertigo or Meniere's disease)?
Do you have trouble with your hearing?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart condition?
Do you feel more unsteady in the dark or at night?
Have you ever had surgery on your back or spine?
Do you ever feel like your feet are stuck to the floor when you start to walk?
Do you have difficulty turning around in bed at night?
Have you noticed that your handwriting has become smaller?
Have you lost your sense of smell in recent years?
Do you have any trouble with your balance when walking on uneven ground or outdoors?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a condition called normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH)?
Do you have a family history of falls or balance problems?
Have you ever had a head injury or concussion?
orders: Get up and go test with detailed observation of gait initiation, turning, and sitting down
Push and release test to assess postural responses
Standing sway test with eyes open and closed
Foot tapping test to assess lower extremity motor function
Brain MRI to assess for structural abnormalities, including the cerebellum, brainstem, and white matter changes

MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio)
